title: End-to-End API Testing
learning_outcomes: Explain how end-to-end api testing affects an API contract or implementation.
Apply the key ideas from testing complete request flows to a concrete API example.
Identify one failure, security, or compatibility risk and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on end-to-end api testing in testing and quality assurance. You will connect testing complete request flows to a concrete API contract decision, inspect a small example, and decide what evidence proves the behavior is correct.
content.why_it_matters: End-to-End API Testing matters because API consumers depend on predictable behavior even when clients, servers, networks, and stored data evolve independently. Applying testing complete request flows deliberately reduces ambiguity, makes failures easier to diagnose, and gives tests a clear expectation.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: High-quality testing verifies both successful behavior and failures at transport, integration, contract, and permission boundaries. In this lesson, treat “End-to-End API Testing” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.

content_blocks.title: Inspect the pattern: End-to-End API Testing
content_blocks.code:
def test_missing_task_returns_404(api_client):
    response = api_client.get("/v1/tasks/does-not-exist")
    assert response.status_code == 404
    assert response.headers["content-type"].startswith("application/problem+json")

# Also test authorization, invalid input, and database failures.
content_blocks.expected_output: The test specifies observable behavior at the API boundary instead of checking internal implementation details.

content_blocks.title: Walkthrough
content_blocks.text: Start with “Testing complete request flows”; it establishes the vocabulary for this topic. Next, compare it with “Creating and updating dependent resources” and “Cleaning test data safely”. In a real API, write down the observable behavior first, then test one normal request and one invalid or unauthorized request. Keep resource state, caller identity, and internal implementation details separate.

content_blocks.title: Professional review check
content_blocks.text: Test failure paths and permission boundaries, not only the happy path. The worked snippet is intentionally inspectable, not an executable hosted API. Replace example.test and placeholder identifiers with local test data only when you implement the lesson project.

content.task: Create a small design note or request/response example demonstrating end-to-end api testing. Use the subtopics above to explain the intended behavior, the main edge case, and the evidence you would use to verify it.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the role of “Testing complete request flows” in this API topic.
Provide a concrete resource, request, response, schema, test, or operational example as appropriate.
Identify one failure/security/compatibility edge case and a test or check for it.
content.expected_output: A reviewable example for End-to-End API Testing with a clear expected behavior and at least one verifiable edge case.
content.run_instructions: Execution mode: static-validation. This lesson example is a protocol, schema, SQL, or code fragment for inspection; it is not submitted to a production server and CodeLeaf does not execute arbitrary learner code. Validate JSON/YAML with a local linter or run the relevant HTTP request against the isolated service you implement for a project. Do not send illustrative example.test requests to a real service.
content.reset_steps: Use a disposable local database or test fixture for implementation work. Restore seed data between runs; never point exercises at production customer data or live payment endpoints.
troubleshooting: Check the exact HTTP method, path, status, header, media type, and payload before changing implementation code.
Separate a transport failure from an application validation failure, authorization denial, and dependency/database failure.
Confirm the example and its client tooling version are compatible; consult the linked standard or official guidance when behavior is ambiguous.
common_mistakes: Treating end-to-end api testing as an implementation detail rather than a documented behavior.
Testing only the happy path and ignoring malformed, unauthorized, conflicting, duplicate, or dependency-failure cases.
Publishing an example without checking version assumptions, sensitive-data exposure, and the expected output.
summary: High-quality testing verifies both successful behavior and failures at transport, integration, contract, and permission boundaries. In this lesson, treat “End-to-End API Testing” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.
Next, connect this idea to Lesson 151: Schema and Contract Testing.
